presets.name: Washington
presets.summary: Pacific storms run into the Olympic Mountains and the Cascades: the windward slopes get metres of rain and over 400 inches of snow a year, and the plateau behind them is semi-arid.

presets.name: Philippines
presets.summary: Northern Luzon: the Habagat monsoon rains and passing typhoons hit the Cordillera Central and the Sierra Madre, while the Cagayan Valley between them is the hottest and driest ground.

presets.name: Tibet
presets.summary: From the Khumbu side of the Himalaya over Everest and the Yarlung Tsangpo valley to the high, cold, dry plateau around Nagqu; the monsoon runs out of moisture long before the north of the plateau.

presets.name: Russia
presets.summary: Moscow across the East European Plain, over the low, old Southern Urals and out onto the flat West Siberian Plain: long cold winters, snow cover for months, Atlantic air that dries out as it goes east.

presets.name: United Kingdom
presets.summary: Atlantic depressions arrive from the south-west: Snowdonia and the Pennines wring out the rain, layered cloud and drizzle are the norm, and the east of England sits in the rain shadow.

presets.name: Central Europe
presets.summary: From the North German Plain over the Harz to the Alpine foreland at Munich and on into the Alps: westerlies, summer thunderstorms on the foreland, föhn on the north side of the range, and snow on the high ground all year.

presets.name: Oklahoma
presets.summary: Tornado Alley: Gulf moisture from the south meets dry air from Mexico and cold air from Canada over the Great Plains, and the storms they breed peak from April to June.

presets.name: Florida
presets.summary: A flat peninsula between two warm seas: a May-October rainy season of daily thunderstorms (more than any other US state), sea breezes, and hurricanes in late summer.

presets.name: Colorado
presets.summary: The Rockies take the Pacific storms' moisture as snow, and the Front Range and the High Plains beyond them sit in the rain shadow with 380-640 mm a year.

presets.name: California
presets.summary: From Monterey Bay across the Central Valley and over the Sierra Nevada to Death Valley: ocean winters in the west, deep snow on the crest, and a desert 86 m below sea level behind it.

presets.name: Alaska
presets.summary: From the Gulf of Alaska coast at Seward up past Anchorage and Denali to Fairbanks: the coast gets metres of snow and rain, the interior behind the Alaska Range is cold and dry.

presets.name: Hawaii
presets.summary: The Big Island under the north-east trade winds: Hilo on the windward side is drenched, the summit of Mauna Kea is dry and snow-capped in winter, and Kona on the lee coast is sheltered.

presets.name: Japan
presets.summary: Honshu from the Sea of Japan over the Japanese Alps and Mount Fuji to Tokyo: the winter north-west monsoon dumps snow on the mountains facing the Sea of Japan and leaves the Pacific side clear, while summer brings the rainy season and typhoons.

presets.name: Meghalaya (India)
presets.summary: The Khasi Hills lie east-west across the monsoon airflow from the Bay of Bengal: Cherrapunji and Mawsynram, on the south face, are among the wettest places on Earth, with a short dry season.

presets.name: Amazon basin (Brazil)
presets.summary: Along the Amazon from the Pico da Neblina past Manaus to Belém: a rainforest that makes half of its own rain, with a wet season and a short drier spell, hot all year.

presets.name: Atacama (Chile)
presets.summary: From the foggy Pacific coast at Antofagasta over the driest desert on Earth to the Andean volcano Licancabur: a two-sided rain shadow where some stations have never recorded rain.

presets.name: Sahara (Algeria)
presets.summary: From the Mediterranean coast at Algiers across the Saharan Atlas and the desert at In Salah to the Hoggar mountains: under 20 mm of rain a year over most of it and the hottest summers on Earth.

presets.name: Kenya and Kilimanjaro
presets.summary: Across the equator from the Tsavo plains past Kilimanjaro and Nairobi to Mount Kenya: two rainy seasons, a cool highland climate, and glaciers on the equator above 4,650 m.

presets.name: Australia
presets.summary: From the Broken Hill outback over the western plains and the Great Dividing Range to Sydney on the Tasman coast: westerly fronts, a mountain barrier that keeps rain off the interior, and an arid heart.

presets.name: New Zealand
presets.summary: The South Island's Southern Alps on the TranzAlpine line: westerly air drops metres of rain on the west coast and crosses Arthur's Pass to a dry Canterbury, where the föhn warms it.

presets.name: Antarctica (McMurdo Sound)
presets.summary: Ross Island and the Transantarctic Mountains around McMurdo Sound: the coast is the warmest part of the continent at about -10 °C, the interior is a cold desert, and katabatic winds pour off the ice.
